findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify what happens to the global deployed-sha ($SHA_FILE) under per-component markers: whether the footer still advances it, how the TARGET=DEPLOYED short-circuit (line 474) is preserved, and how the config/obs/certbot blocks (504/728/751) that still diff from $DEPLOYED are reconciled with the new bot/mcp markers.
evidence: Plan: 'each component's delta gate RE-POINTED to diff from its own marker rather than the global $DEPLOYED baseline. An absent or unparseable marker falls back to $DEPLOYED.'
autodeploy.sh:474 `if [ "$TARGET" = "$DEPLOYED" ]; then ... exit 0` short-circuits the whole tick before any component block runs
autodeploy.sh:763 `echo "$TARGET" > "$SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv ...` advances the single global marker at the footer
autodeploy.sh:504/728/751 the config-detect, obs, and certbot blocks still call `changed()` which diffs `$DEPLOYED` -> `$TARGET`
findings.finding: The 'Shape of the fix' re-points only the BOT and MCP delta gates to per-component markers but does not specify the continued role of the global deployed-sha ($SHA_FILE): whether/when the footer still advances it, how the top-level 'up to date' short-circuit (TARGET=DEPLOYED, line 474) behaves once per-component markers can lag the global one, and how the config/obs/certbot blocks that still diff from $DEPLOYED are affected.
scenarios: If the footer keeps advancing the global deployed-sha whenever the tick completes, the 474 short-circuit fires on the next tick and the per-component markers can never trigger a redeploy — nullifying the completion fix.
If the footer stops advancing the global marker, the up-to-date no-op (474) and the config/obs/certbot changed() diffs (504/728/751) never converge and re-fire every tick.

tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py:208/229/506 assert deployed-sha value after defer/success/burst

Plan does not state whether state/deployed-sha is retained as the footer target or replaced by the two per-component markers
findings.finding: The completion-marker split re-points delta gates to mcp-deployed-sha/bot-deployed-sha and gates the footer on *_incomplete, but several tests assert on state/deployed-sha for deploy completion / non-advancement; the plan does not state whether the footer still writes deployed-sha, leaving these consumers of the completion semantics unenumerated.
findings.location: Plan § 'Shape of the fix' (mcp-deployed-sha / bot-deployed-sha bullet) and § 'Consumers outside autodeploy.sh'
scenarios: If the footer stops writing state/deployed-sha in favour of per-component markers, every test asserting on state/deployed-sha (health_gate, review_drain, mcp_bluegreen) reads a stale/absent file and must be updated; if deployed-sha is kept, the plan should say so.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the consumers section: state whether the footer continues to write state/deployed-sha (keeping these tests green) or writes only the two per-component markers (requiring those tests to be re-pointed), matching the prune-consumer treatment.

findings.finding: The plan makes the incompleteness/completion guarantees depend on new marker file writes (mcp-deployed-sha, bot-deployed-sha, and bot_incomplete/mcp_incomplete flags) written 'the moment that component completes', but does not state whether these writes are atomic/durable against a mid-tick crash or partial write — the very failure the incompleteness fix aims to close could recur if a marker write is torn.
findings.location: Shape of the fix (marker writes) / incompleteness bullet
scenarios: autodeploy is killed after deploying mcp but before/while writing mcp-deployed-sha, leaving stale state that re-triggers the harm the drain gate prevents

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the new per-component marker and backoff files are overwritten-in-place (bounded, one per component) and therefore do not accumulate — or add a cleanup note if a component is ever retired.
evidence: Plan introduces 'mcp-deployed-sha and bot-deployed-sha' and 'a separate mcp-deploy-backoff recorder' but no section addresses their retirement or bounded growth.
T9(d) requires a RETIRE/cleanup path or evidence the state does not leak/accumulate.
findings.finding: The plan defines CREATE, UPDATE, and CONSUME for the three new state files (mcp-deployed-sha, bot-deployed-sha, mcp-deploy-backoff) but never states a RETIRE/cleanup path or confirms they cannot accumulate. They appear bounded (one per component, overwritten in place), but this is left implicit.
findings.location: Shape of the fix (new marker/backoff files)
scenarios: A future component removal or renaming leaves an orphaned marker/backoff file in state/ that no code cleans up.
An operator inspecting state/ cannot tell whether stale markers are live or abandoned.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to 'Shape of the fix' noting each marker/backoff file is a single overwritten path per component (bounded), so there is no accumulation, and nothing to retire while the component exists.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rollback path: reverting autodeploy.sh restores the global-state behavior, and leftover per-component marker/backoff files are inert (ignored by the old code), so no state cleanup is required.
evidence: Plan changes runtime behavior of autodeploy.sh, a live deploy script ('a larger restructure of a live deploy script').
T12(b) asks for an explicit, cheap, tested way to undo quickly without data cleanup; the plan does not state one.
findings.finding: This is a behavior change to a live deploy orchestrator (autodeploy.sh) but the plan states no explicit rollback path. Old+new coexistence is handled (absent marker falls back to $DEPLOYED), yet reverting the change is not described — e.g. whether leftover new state files harm a reverted-to-old-code tick.
findings.location: Deliberately out of scope / Shape of the fix
scenarios: A regression forces reverting autodeploy.sh: an operator is unsure whether the newly-written mcp-deployed-sha / mcp-deploy-backoff files must be removed for the old code path to behave correctly.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line rollback note confirming the revert is a pure code revert with no state cleanup, since the old code reads only the global deployed-sha/deploy-backoff and ignores the new files.
